rubric.scope: Private life science companies raising $1M–$52M (with tolerance band to $57M)
rubric.not_for: Due diligence, portfolio management, scientific merit evaluation

section.name: Evaluation Context
section.block: This is a two-profile Ideal Company Profile (ICP) scoring instrument built for a fundraiser to use as a top-of-funnel qualification and prioritization tool. Its purpose is to evaluate private life science companies (biotech, medtech, diagnostics, pharma) that are actively seeking capital in the $1M–$52M range and produce a structured, scored assessment of each company's probability of successfully closing a funding round. This instrument is not a due diligence tool and was not designed for portfolio management, scientific merit evaluation, or investment decision-making.

The rubric is explicitly built to identify companies that can raise money most easily — not companies with the best science or most promising products. Scientific promise and fundraising ease diverge meaningfully in practice. The evaluation target is investor psychology, deal velocity, and capital market dynamics. Every criterion, weight, and scoring band is calibrated against this objective. STANDING INSTRUCTION: The objective is fundraising velocity and investor appetite — not scientific promise. Score accordingly.

block.name: Client Specifications
block.spec: Series B (100%), Series A (95%), Seed (40%), Pre-Seed (excluded at 90%)
Single most important criterion. Strong preference for industry veterans and serial entrepreneurs. Academic spinouts deprioritized (negative signal, not automatic disqualifier).
Sporadic or messy cap tables are a hard disqualifier across both profiles.
Preferred but not a hard requirement.
No hard requirements specified; rubric applies best-practice expectations appropriate to each profile's development stage.

section.block: The $1M–$52M range is split into Profile A ($30M–$52M) and Profile B ($1M–$15M) to create meaningful separation between two genuinely different fundraising environments. FDA regulatory pathway stage and clinical development phase serve as the product viability anchor for both profiles because they are verifiable, stage-specific, and directly correlated with investor risk tolerance at each funding level.

When information for a criterion is insufficient to produce a confident score, assign the midpoint of the applicable scoring band and flag the score with [INSUFFICIENT DATA]. Do not penalize companies for missing information below the midpoint. This protocol applies to all criteria in both profiles. The Data Confidence indicator in Section 5 aggregates these flags to provide an overall assessment of score reliability.
MIDPOINT-DEFAULT JUSTIFICATION STANDARD: When the midpoint-default is applied to a criterion, the Justification field must do more than cite protocol application. The evaluator must articulate why the midpoint — rather than a score above or below midpoint within the band — is appropriate given whatever partial evidence exists. If partial evidence supports a score above or below the midpoint, score accordingly and document the partial evidence. Reserve the exact midpoint for situations where evidence is genuinely absent and no directional signal is available.
INFORMATION-SCARCE vs. INFORMATION-ABSENT CLASSIFICATION:
Before applying the midpoint-default to any criterion, the evaluator must classify the missing information as one of two types:
INFORMATION-SCARCE: Evidence exists that the company has engaged in the activity measured by this criterion — for example, the company has employees but their backgrounds are not publicly detailed; the company has raised capital but terms are undisclosed; the company has filed IP but the filings are not yet public; the company has conducted experiments but results are not released. The existence of the underlying activity is supported by some observable signal, even if the details are not available. When information is SCARCE: apply the midpoint-default as specified in this section. Flag as [INSUFFICIENT DATA — INFORMATION-SCARCE]. In the Justification field, state the observable signal that confirms the underlying activity exists.
INFORMATION-ABSENT: No evidence exists that the company has engaged in the activity measured by this criterion — for example, no publications because no science has been produced; no patents because no IP has been generated; no grants because none have been applied for or received; no confirmed employees because none may exist; no product demonstrations because no product has been built. The absence is not caused by non-disclosure of existing information but by the non-existence of the things the information would describe. When information is ABSENT: score in the lowest applicable band per the band definitions. The midpoint-default does not apply. Flag as [INSUFFICIENT DATA — INFORMATION-ABSENT] and document in the Justification field: (a) what evidence was searched for, (b) why the absence is classified as information-absent rather than information-scarce, and (c) the specific band assigned and its justification.
AMBIGUOUS CASES: When partial evidence exists but it is ambiguous whether the underlying activity has occurred, default to INFORMATION-SCARCE and document the ambiguity. The INFORMATION-ABSENT classification should only be applied when the evaluator has actively searched for evidence of the underlying activity across available sources and found none.
INTERACTION WITH B4 MILESTONE SCORING GUIDANCE: The B4 milestone scoring guidance (Scenario A — no milestone plan disclosed) is a specialized application of the INFORMATION-SCARCE classification. Seed-stage companies commonly do not publicly disclose milestone plans; the absence of a disclosed plan is presumed to be non-disclosure of an existing plan unless evidence indicates otherwise. If the evaluator has reason to believe the company has no milestone plan (e.g., the company appears pre-operational across multiple criteria), the INFORMATION-ABSENT classification may be applied to B4 with documentation of the basis.

Any deviation from the client's original specifications in the scoring criteria, weights, or band definitions must be documented in a Market Context Note at the point of deviation. The evaluator has latitude to adjust, reorder, replace, or add criteria relative to the original specifications, provided deviations are disclosed.

Both profiles score on a base scale of 100 points. The Market-Evidence Modifier on the Sector criterion (A3/B3) can adjust the total by up to ±2 points, producing a scoring range of 96–102 points. Fundability tier thresholds are defined in absolute point values and apply across the full scoring range.
DESIGN CONSTRAINT: This instrument uses an additive, independent-criterion scoring architecture. When a single development (such as a strategic pivot or regulatory event) affects multiple criteria simultaneously, the independent scoring structure cannot express the correlated risk quantitatively. Evaluators should describe cross-criterion risk correlations qualitatively in the Top 3 Fundability Risks (Block 5) and Fundraising Outlook (Block 5) sections of the output. The quantitative scores for each criterion remain independently assessed per their respective band definitions.
CROSS-CRITERION SYMMETRY: When a single risk affects multiple criteria and appears in multiple Top 3 Fundability Risk entries in Block 5, each risk entry must note the correlation to the other affected criteria. A cross-criterion risk described from only one direction understates its aggregate impact on the evaluation.

section.name: Routing Logic
section.block:
Every company evaluated under this instrument must first be routed to Profile A or Profile B. Routing is based on the company's most recent completed funding round size, its current fundraising target (if known), and its clinical/regulatory development stage. The routing decision is made before any criterion is scored.
Assign to Profile A if the company's target raise is $30M–$52M, or if the most recent completed round was $20M or above and the current raise is expected to be at or above $30M. Profile A companies are typically at IND-filed, Phase 1, or Phase 2 stage with institutional venture syndicate involvement and formal board governance. Profile A expects more advanced regulatory and clinical maturity, experienced management teams with prior exits, and institutional-quality cap tables.
Assign to Profile B if the company's target raise is $1M–$15M, or if total capital raised to date is under $20M and the company is at discovery, preclinical, or early IND-enabling stage. Profile B companies may include seed-stage, accelerator-graduated, or early institutional-round companies. Profile B expects earlier-stage positioning with upside potential, scientific founder credibility, and emerging validation signals.
Companies targeting $15M–$30M fall in the gap between profiles. Route to Profile A if the company has IND-filed or later-stage clinical assets, institutional VC leads, and an experienced management team. Route to Profile B if the company is at preclinical or early IND-enabling stage with a scientific founder team and limited institutional infrastructure. If the routing is ambiguous, conduct a split evaluation under both profiles and report the score range.

The instrument is calibrated for private capital markets. Publicly traded companies and pre-seed companies (total raised under $500K with no institutional participation) are OUT OF SCOPE. An OUT OF SCOPE flag is a scope/instrument mismatch, not a disqualifying deficiency. Out-of-scope companies may be evaluated as benchmark exercises if clearly flagged.
Companies whose target raise is $52M or below are IN SCOPE. Companies whose target raise exceeds $52M but is at or below $57.2M (10% above the $52M ceiling) are classified as GRAY ZONE. Gray Zone companies are evaluated under the appropriate profile with a mandatory Gray Zone scope flag in the output. The evaluator must note the overshoot in the Routing Rationale and acknowledge that the instrument's calibration may be less precise for raises above $52M. Companies whose target raise exceeds $57.2M are OUT OF SCOPE and may only be evaluated as benchmark exercises with an Out of Scope — Benchmark flag.
The instrument is calibrated for therapeutic life science companies with clinical and regulatory development pathways (biotech, pharma, medtech, diagnostics with therapeutic intent). Non-therapeutic life science companies — including bioinformatics software, genomic data infrastructure, health IT platforms, life science tools, and diagnostic software without a companion therapeutic — are within the general life science scope of the instrument but produce persistent band language friction, most notably on B2 (Scientific Foundation and Data Package) and B7 (IP and Technology Defensibility), and require sector classification via the Health IT / Genomics Infrastructure / Life Science Tools addition in A3/B3.
The v4.0 non-therapeutic application notes on B1, B2, and B7, and the Health IT / Genomics Infrastructure / Life Science Tools sector addition on A3/B3, collectively provide an analog framework for evaluating non-therapeutic companies. This framework is a documented boundary condition of the instrument, not a rubric deficiency. Evaluations of non-therapeutic companies conducted under this framework remain valid but carry lower rubric fit than evaluations of therapeutic companies. Evaluators must document the non-therapeutic classification in the Block 1 Market Context Note field, identify which criteria required analog application, and note that rubric fit limitations apply.
Clients whose target pipeline exceeds approximately 20% non-therapeutic companies should consider commissioning a dedicated Profile C track calibrated to non-therapeutic fundability signals — including ARR, customer concentration, sales cycle compression, platform defensibility, category leadership, and applicable regulatory pathway (510k, De Novo, LDT). See Future Revisions entry FV-3 for the deferred Profile C design direction. Until such a track is developed, non-therapeutic companies continue to be evaluated under the analog framework with the boundary condition flagged in the Market Context Note.
Target raise falls within the $1M–$52M range. Standard evaluation applies. Target raise exceeds $52M but is at or below $57.2M (10% tolerance). Evaluation proceeds under the appropriate profile with a mandatory acknowledgment that instrument calibration may be less precise. Target raise exceeds $57.2M, or company is publicly traded, or company is pre-seed. Evaluation may proceed as a benchmark exercise if clearly flagged. Scores should not be compared directly to in-scope evaluations.

The following conditions trigger automatic disqualification regardless of score. A disqualified company is classified as Out of Scope and does not receive a fundability tier assignment. If any disqualifier is triggered, the evaluation terminates after the Disqualifier Screen (Block 2 of the output format). No criterion scores, total score, or fundability tier are assigned. A score below 40 with no disqualifier triggered is classified as Tier 4 — Not Ready, not as Out of Scope. Out of Scope status is reserved for instrument scope mismatches and disqualifier triggers. Sporadic, messy, or structurally compromised cap table with unresolved ownership disputes, missing documentation, or legal encumbrances (applies to both profiles). Active FDA enforcement action (Warning Letter, clinical hold without resolution pathway, consent decree) that materially impairs the lead program's development timeline. NOT APPLICABLE TO NON-THERAPEUTIC COMPANIES: This disqualifier applies only to companies with FDA-regulated therapeutic assets, medical devices, or diagnostics. For non-therapeutic companies (bioinformatics software, health IT, life science tools, genomic data platforms), mark this disqualifier as "NOT APPLICABLE" rather than "CLEAR." Marking NOT APPLICABLE does not trigger disqualification. See the alternative disqualifier below for non-therapeutic companies. Active data security enforcement action — including a consent order, corrective action plan, or equivalent regulatory mandate from a data protection authority (HHS Office for Civil Rights under HIPAA, EU/UK data protection authorities under GDPR, or equivalent) — that materially impairs the company's ability to operate, retain customers, or handle protected health information or genomic data. Applies to non-therapeutic companies handling protected health information, genomic data, or other regulated data categories. NOT APPLICABLE TO THERAPEUTIC COMPANIES with no data handling regulatory exposure; mark as "NOT APPLICABLE" for such companies. Pending or unresolved material litigation that creates existential risk to the company's operations or IP position. Founder or C-suite executive subject to active SEC enforcement, FDA debarment, or criminal proceedings related to securities fraud or scientific misconduct.

criterion.name: Team Quality and Execution Credibility
criterion.purpose: Evaluates the founding and executive team's demonstrated ability to build, advance, and exit life science companies. Measures direct signals of fundraising credibility: prior exit experience, domain expertise at the relevant development stage, board-level VC representation, and KOL advisory network density. Single most heavily weighted criterion per client specification.
criterion.band: At least one C-suite member (CEO, CSO, CMO, or CFO) with a confirmed exit above $500M in the life sciences sector. Domain-expert CSO or CMO with direct IND-or-later clinical development history in the company's therapeutic area. At least one top-tier life science VC partner (Third Rock, ARCH, Flagship, Sofinnova, OrbiMed, 5AM, Versant, or equivalent) on the board of directors. Scientific Advisory Board includes recognized KOLs from leading academic medical centers or research institutions. CEO with prior experience as a biotech C-suite executive (not first-time founder at this raise level).

C-suite includes executives with prior biotech operating experience but no confirmed exits above $500M. Domain expertise present but may not include direct IND+ clinical development in the specific therapeutic area. Board includes institutional VC representation but not necessarily top-tier life science specialists. Advisory board exists with relevant scientific or clinical experts. CEO may be a first-time biotech CEO with strong prior functional leadership roles.

Team includes relevant scientific or clinical expertise but limited biotech operating experience. No confirmed exits among leadership. Board representation is present but lacks institutional VC with life science specialization. Advisory board is informal or undisclosed. CEO may be an academic founder or first-time operator without prior C-suite experience.

Team is primarily academic with no biotech operating or commercial experience. No institutional board members. No formal advisory board. No confirmed fundraising track record among leadership. Academic spinout with undisclosed or non-existent governance structure.
criterion.negative_credibility_protocol:
NEGATIVE CREDIBILITY SIGNAL PROTOCOL: Before finalizing the A1 score, the evaluator must assess whether any credibility claims made by the team — including titles, institutional affiliations, authorship or contribution claims, priority claims, and competitive positioning claims — are directly contradicted by verifiable evidence. Verifiable evidence includes: title records (LinkedIn, company website, filings); publication author lists (PubMed, bioRxiv, journal archives); public regulatory records (FDA, EMA, Companies House); and direct competitive existence data (competitor websites, press releases, third-party databases).
If one or more contradictions are identified, apply a deduction within the assigned band as follows:
SINGLE MINOR CONTRADICTION: A single instance of informal title inflation, modest overstatement of a contribution, or unverifiable but plausible claim. Apply a 1-point deduction within the assigned band. Do not drop below the band floor.
MULTIPLE CONTRADICTIONS OR SINGLE MATERIAL CONTRADICTION: Multiple contradicted claims, or a single materially false claim (fabricated institutional affiliation, false authorship claim, claimed contribution to a public law or regulatory process that is contradicted by the public record). Apply a 2–3 point deduction within the assigned band. The evaluator may drop to the next lower band if the deduction would exceed the band floor.
NO CONTRADICTIONS IDENTIFIED: No deduction. Score per band definitions on their merits.
This protocol applies regardless of whether the midpoint-default is in effect. A score at the band midpoint under the midpoint-default may still receive a deduction if contradicted claims are identified with verifiable evidence.
DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENT: The Justification field must name each contradiction, identify the source that contradicts it, and state the deduction applied. When no contradictions are found, a one-sentence statement is sufficient: "Negative Credibility Signal Protocol applied — no contradicted claims identified."

criterion.name: Clinical/Regulatory Stage and Data Quality
criterion.purpose: Evaluates the maturity of the company's lead clinical program based on regulatory stage progression and the quality of available clinical or preclinical data. Measures development milestones that directly correlate with investor risk tolerance. Does NOT score FDA designations — see A4.

band.label: Advanced Clinical Stage with Strong Data

criterion.band: Lead asset is in Phase 2 or later with topline efficacy data in hand. Data demonstrates statistically significant primary endpoint results (p<0.05) in a well-powered or signal-generating study. End-of-Phase 2 meeting completed or Phase 3 design aligned with FDA. No unresolved clinical holds on the lead program. Safety profile is clean or manageable with no serious adverse event signals that would impair regulatory path. Multiple clinical trials completed or in progress (Phase 1 safety, PK/PD, and efficacy studies).

band.label: Mid-Clinical Stage or Early Efficacy Signals

criterion.band: Lead asset is in Phase 1b/2a or Phase 2 with preliminary efficacy signals but topline data not yet in hand, or data is from a small open-label study requiring confirmation. IND is filed and accepted. At least one Phase 1 trial completed with acceptable safety. Pre-IND or IND meeting with FDA completed with documented alignment on development plan. Clinical hold history, if any, has been resolved.

band.label: IND-Stage or Late Preclinical with Regulatory Engagement

criterion.band: IND filed or IND-enabling studies substantially complete. Pre-IND meeting held or scheduled with FDA. Preclinical efficacy data in validated animal models with dose-response relationships. Safety/toxicology package in preparation or completed. No clinical data yet available. Development path to Phase 1 is defined with estimated timelines.

Discovery or early preclinical stage. In vitro data only, or animal model data without regulatory-grade toxicology. No FDA engagement. IND filing timeline is undefined or more than 18 months away. Lead candidate selection may not be finalized.

criterion.name: Sector and Market Alignment
criterion.purpose: Evaluates whether the company operates in a therapeutic sector currently attracting active investor capital and M&A interest. Uses a two-component structure: base tier classification (general investor appetite) plus market-evidence modifier (recent documented deal activity).

component.name: Base Tier Classification
component.band: Company operates in a sector with demonstrated peak-level capital deployment in the current fundraising cycle. Tier 1 sectors for 2025–2026: obesity/GLP-1 and metabolic therapies; antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) and targeted oncology payloads; radiopharmaceuticals; immunology/inflammation; AI-native drug discovery platforms. Company's addressable market exceeds $2B in the primary indication. Platform technology with multi-indication optionality in Tier 1 therapeutic areas.

Company operates in a sector with active but not peak-level investor interest. Tier 2 sectors for 2025–2026: neuroscience/CNS; rare disease; gene therapy and cell therapy; cardiovascular; precision oncology (non-ADC). Addressable market exceeds $1B. First-in-class or differentiated mechanism within the Tier 2 sector. Multiple potential acquirers identifiable.
component.sector_addition: HEALTH IT / GENOMICS INFRASTRUCTURE / LIFE SCIENCE TOOLS — TIER 2 DEFAULT: Companies providing software platforms, data infrastructure, analytical tools, or enabling technologies to the life science industry — including but not limited to: bioinformatics software; genomic data management and compression platforms; laboratory information management systems (LIMS); clinical trial management software; drug discovery computational platforms; regulatory affairs software; and diagnostic decision-support tools — are classified as Tier 2 by default unless specific market evidence supports a different classification. Tier 2 classification for health IT and life science tools companies reflects active but not peak-level investor interest in this category for the 2025–2026 cycle. A Tier 1 upgrade may be applied if the platform is explicitly positioned as an AI-native drug discovery tool (which falls under the Tier 1 AI-native platform definition) or if documented exceptional sector M&A activity in the specific tools category supports the upgrade. A Tier 3 downgrade may be applied if the investor universe for the specific tool category is demonstrably narrow or if the platform competes primarily against free, open-source, or bundled alternatives with no clear path to premium monetization.
component.band: Company operates in a sector with limited or specialized investor interest. Includes: anti-infectives/antibiotics; women's health; diagnostics without companion therapeutic; agricultural biotech. Addressable market below $1B or market size uncertain. Investor universe is narrow and may require specialized fund targeting.
Company operates in a sector with minimal current investor appetite, or the sector category is too early or undefined to classify. No identifiable recent M&A or IPO activity in the sector.

component.name: Market-Evidence Modifier
component.instruction: After assigning the base tier score, apply the following modifier based on documented sector-specific M&A activity, capital deployment, and deal flow within the 12 months preceding the evaluation date. The modifier adjusts the base score and may cause the final A3 score to exceed the base tier ceiling or fall below the base tier floor.
component.modifier: Three or more acquisitions exceeding $1B occurred in the company's specific sector within the past 12 months. Sector is attracting capital at historically elevated levels. Multiple large pharma companies actively deploying capital through M&A, licensing, or CVC investment.

One to two acquisitions exceeding $1B occurred in the sector within the past 12 months, or significant licensing/partnership deal flow demonstrates rising investor interest. Sector activity is above its historical baseline but not at peak levels.
Sector M&A and capital deployment activity is consistent with the base tier classification. No significant deviation from expected deal flow. The base tier score stands without adjustment.

Sector has experienced notable funding contraction, major pipeline failures, or clinical trial setbacks within the past 12 months that have dampened investor appetite. One or more high-profile failures in the sector have increased perceived risk.

Sector has experienced systemic capital withdrawal, regulatory headwinds affecting the entire therapeutic class, or a pattern of clinical failures that has materially reduced investor willingness to deploy capital. Fund allocation to the sector has declined measurably.

criterion.operational_viability_condition:
OPERATIONAL VIABILITY CONDITION: Before finalizing the A3 score, apply the following gate.
TRIGGER: If the company scores in its lowest defined band on BOTH A2 (Clinical/Regulatory Stage and Data Quality, Band 0–7) AND A4 (Validation Signals and Partnerships, Band 0–3), the A3 final score (base tier score plus any market-evidence modifier) is capped at 8 points.
RATIONALE: At the Profile A raise level, Band 0–7 on A2 ("Early Preclinical or Pre-IND") indicates the company has not yet entered clinical development; Band 0–3 on A4 ("Minimal or No External Validation") indicates no pharma partnerships, no conference presence, no FDA designation activity, and no grants. When both conditions are met simultaneously, the company has demonstrated neither minimum clinical/regulatory maturity nor minimum external endorsement, and the structural reality is that sector conditions cannot be monetized. The AND condition prevents penalizing companies with genuine clinical-stage progress that lack external validation signals (or vice versa).
CAP VALUE: 8 points (the Tier 3 band ceiling for A3).
DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENT: When the Operational Viability Condition is triggered, document in the A3 Justification field: (a) the A2 and A4 scores that triggered the cap, (b) the uncapped A3 score that would have applied, and (c) the capped score that is recorded. When the condition is not triggered, a one-sentence confirmation is sufficient: "Operational Viability Condition not triggered — A2=[X] and/or A4=[X] above threshold."

criterion.name: Validation Signals and Partnerships
criterion.status: Revised — V.5 R1; prior revisions retained
criterion.purpose: Evaluates external validation signals that independently confirm the company's fundraising attractiveness: partnership quality, conference presence, FDA designations, and pharma commercial engagement. These signals reduce perceived risk and accelerate due diligence timelines. This is the sole criterion that scores FDA special designations.
criterion.cvc_routing_instruction: When a corporate venture capital (CVC) arm of a pharma or strategic company has invested in the company and/or taken a board seat, the signal should be routed as follows: The strategic validation dimension of the CVC relationship — meaning the implied endorsement of the company's science, platform, or therapeutic approach by the CVC's parent company — is scored under A4. The financial participation dimension — meaning the CVC's presence on the cap table, its follow-on capacity, and its contribution to syndicate quality — is scored under A5. If the CVC has both invested and taken a board seat, both A4 and A5 may reflect the CVC signal, but for different aspects. The evaluator must not double-count the same dimension of the signal across both criteria.
criterion.band: Active pharma commercial validation evidenced by one or more of: executed licensing deals with upfront payments, co-development agreements, CVC investment with documented strategic rationale, or formal strategic partnership engagement with a large pharma counterparty. A single high-quality commercial validation signal is sufficient for this band. Top-tier medical or investor conference presentations (JPM Healthcare, ASCO, AAN, ASH, AACR, or equivalent sector-specific venue) at two or more events. FDA special designation received or publicly announced (Fast Track, Breakthrough Therapy, Orphan Drug, or Accelerated Approval pathway) for the lead program. Sell-side analyst coverage initiated by two or more banks.

At least one executed pharma partnership or licensing deal (may lack upfront payment or may be at the CRO/co-development level rather than full commercial license). Conference presentations at recognized but not necessarily top-tier venues, or a single top-tier presentation. FDA pre-designation engagement (pre-IND meeting with designation discussion) or designation application filed but not yet received. Some sell-side or investor awareness but limited formal coverage.

Informal pharma engagement or documented strategic interest without executed deals. Conference poster presentations or accepted abstracts. No FDA designation received or filed. Non-dilutive grant funding (NIH, BARDA, SBIR/STTR) received as an alternative validation signal. Media coverage or industry recognition without formal institutional endorsement.

No pharma partnerships, no conference presentations at recognized venues, no FDA designation activity, no non-dilutive grants, and no institutional recognition signals. Company is operating in stealth or has not yet engaged with the broader pharma and investor ecosystem.

criterion.name: Cap Table and Investor Base Quality
criterion.purpose: Evaluates the quality, structure, and institutional depth of the company's existing investor base. A strong cap table reduces re-syndication risk, signals insider conviction, and accelerates new investor due diligence. A messy or structurally compromised cap table is a hard disqualifier (see Section 2.3). For CVC signal routing, see A4's CVC routing instruction — A5 captures the financial participation dimension of CVC investment.
criterion.band: Cap table led by top-tier life science VCs (Third Rock, ARCH, Flagship, Sofinnova, OrbiMed, Versant, 5AM, or equivalent). Strategic CVC participation from a relevant large pharma company. Crossover investors present or committed (Perceptive, RA Capital, Cormorant, Foresite, Fidelity, T. Rowe Price, or equivalent). Existing investors committed pro-rata in subsequent rounds, demonstrating insider conviction. Cap table is clean with no structural complexity, no outstanding convertible instruments with adverse terms, and no unresolved ownership disputes.

Cap table includes recognized life science VCs but not necessarily top-tier names. At least one institutional lead with demonstrated follow-on capacity. Pro-rata participation from existing investors in prior rounds. No structural cap table issues. CVC participation may be absent.

Cap table includes a mix of institutional and angel investors. Lead investor may be a generalist VC or a smaller life science fund. Follow-on capacity of existing investors is uncertain. Cap table structure is acceptable but may have minor complexity (multiple SAFE instruments, convertible notes with varying terms). No disqualifying issues.

Cap table is primarily angel or friends-and-family with no institutional participation. Lead investor is absent or unidentifiable. Cap table may have structural issues that require cleanup before an institutional round. Score of 0 indicates a cap table that approaches but does not trigger the automatic disqualifier.

criterion.name: Deal Structure and Fundraising Mechanics
criterion.status: Revised — V.5 R1; v5.1 R1; prior revisions retained
criterion.purpose: Evaluates the mechanics of the company's fundraising: round structure, use-of-proceeds clarity, runway sufficiency, and the quality of capital raise execution. Also evaluates strategic coherence between the company's pitch materials and its observable behavior. Measures operational signals that investors evaluate during term sheet negotiation and closing.

strategic_coherence_assessment.instruction: Before scoring the band definitions below, the evaluator must assess whether any material post-pitch development has occurred that contradicts the company's stated use of proceeds, business model, or strategic direction as presented in its pitch materials or most recent investor communications. Material post-pitch developments include but are not limited to: strategic pivots to a different business model or market; significant layoffs affecting key functions (clinical, regulatory, CMC); discontinuation or deprioritization of the lead program referenced in the use of proceeds; announced changes to the company's core technology platform or therapeutic focus.
strategic_coherence_assessment.scoring_impact:
If a material post-pitch development is identified that directly contradicts the stated use of proceeds, the evaluator must apply a scoring penalty within the A6 band assignment. The severity of the penalty depends on the degree of contradiction:
SEVERE CONTRADICTION — The company's observable strategic direction is fundamentally inconsistent with its stated use of proceeds (e.g., pivot away from the therapeutic area or development stage that the raise is designed to fund). Apply the scoring rule as follows: (1) Default — score at the floor of the applicable band. (2) Drop to the top of the next lower band only when the non-SCA deal mechanics signals (round structure, use-of-proceeds mapping before the contradiction, prior capital efficiency, runway) independently warrant the lower band. (3) If the non-SCA signals warrant a score below the lower band's top, score at the assessed position within that lower band. A severe contradiction must always be flagged as a Top 3 Fundability Risk in Block 5 of the output, and the Justification field must explicitly state which rule (1, 2, or 3) was applied and why.
MODERATE CONTRADICTION — The company has made material changes to its strategy or operations that partially undermine confidence in the stated use of proceeds but do not fundamentally invalidate the fundraising thesis (e.g., reprioritization of pipeline assets, organizational restructuring that delays but does not cancel the stated milestones). Apply a 1-2 point deduction within the applicable band.
MINOR OR NO CONTRADICTION — The company's observable behavior is consistent with its stated use of proceeds, or any operational changes are immaterial to the fundraising thesis. No adjustment. Score the band definitions below on their merits.
strategic_coherence_assessment.documentation_requirement: DOCUMENTATION REQUIRED REGARDLESS OF OUTCOME: The Strategic Coherence Assessment must be documented in the A6/B6 Justification field for every evaluation, regardless of whether a contradiction is found. When the determination is Minor or No Contradiction, include a one-sentence statement in the following form: "Strategic Coherence Assessment: [brief description of what was reviewed — e.g., pitch materials, press releases, website, post-pitch announcements]. Determination: Minor or No Contradiction — no adjustment applied." Silent omission of the assessment is not permitted. An undocumented assessment cannot be verified and will be flagged as a format violation in any subsequent performance audit.

criterion.band: Current or most recent round was cleanly structured (priced equity round or well-structured convertible with standard terms). Use of proceeds is mapped to specific, identifiable milestones (clinical trial milestones, regulatory submissions, key hires). Cash runway extends at least 18–24 months past the current raise at projected burn rate. Prior rounds demonstrated capital efficiency (milestones achieved relative to capital deployed). Bookrunner or placement agent of institutional quality is engaged, if applicable.

Round structure is acceptable but may lack full institutional polish (e.g., convertible note without a cap, or SAFE terms that are nonstandard). Use of proceeds is directionally clear but not mapped to specific milestones. Runway extends 12–18 months. Prior capital efficiency is adequate but not exceptional.

Round structure has notable complexity or nonstandard terms that may slow institutional investor participation. Use of proceeds is vague or overly general. Runway is under 12 months or dependent on the current raise closing quickly. Capital efficiency in prior rounds is unclear.

No identifiable round structure or terms. Use of proceeds is undisclosed. Runway is critically short (under 6 months). No evidence of prior fundraising execution quality. Company may be in a distressed capital position.

criterion.name: Competitive Positioning and Exit Pathway
criterion.purpose: Evaluates the company's competitive differentiation and the visibility of its exit pathway. Measures whether identifiable acquirers exist, whether comparable transactions support the company's implied valuation, and whether competitive positioning enhances or impairs attractiveness to exit-oriented investors.
criterion.band: Company has a first-in-class or best-in-class asset with no approved mechanism competition. At least one comparable M&A transaction above $1B at a similar development stage has occurred within the past 3 years. Multiple identifiable acquirers exist based on sector fit, pipeline gaps, and disclosed BD priorities. Company is already on acquirer watch lists or has received documented inbound interest.

Company has a differentiated mechanism or approach but faces competition from 1–2 programs at similar or more advanced stages. Comparable transactions exist but may not be at the same development stage or valuation range. Potential acquirers are identifiable but the exit pathway is not as clear. Competitive dynamics add risk but do not block the path.

Company operates in a crowded therapeutic space with multiple competitors at similar or more advanced stages. Comparable exits exist but at lower valuations or earlier stages. Exit pathway is uncertain or dependent on competitive outcomes. Differentiation from existing programs is limited.

Company's mechanism is not clearly differentiated from existing approved therapies or advanced competitors. No comparable exit transactions identified. Acquirer universe is narrow or non-existent. The company does not present a compelling exit thesis to investors.

criterion.name: Team Quality and Execution Credibility
criterion.status: Revised — V.5 R3; prior revisions retained
criterion.purpose: Evaluates the founding and executive team's credibility as a fundraising signal at the $1M–$15M level. Emphasizes scientific founder credibility, KOL network access, and early signals of commercial translation capability. Industry operating experience carries positive weight but is not expected at the same density as Profile A.
criterion.band: At least one C-suite member with a confirmed life science exit above $500M. Domain-expert CSO or CMO with direct IND-or-later clinical development history in the company's therapeutic area. Industry CEO or COO with biotech operating experience at a company that reached clinical stage or later. Board includes at least one institutional VC with life science specialization. Formal Scientific Advisory Board with recognized KOLs. This band is rare at Profile B raise levels and indicates a team that could credibly lead a Profile A raise.

band.label: Strong Academic Credibility with Industry Gaps

criterion.band:
Scientific founder or co-founder with deep domain expertise and KOL network access. No confirmed prior exits among founders. No industry operating CEO with pharma/biotech commercial or regulatory leadership experience. Advisory board may be informal or undisclosed. The absence of industry operating experience is expected at this raise level but represents a gap that Series A investors at $30M+ will require to be filled.
Academic founders who are world-class KOLs with major discovery contributions directly underlying the company's platform; hold leadership positions at tier-one research institutions (director-level or above); or have publications in top-tier journals (Science, Nature, Cell, NEJM, Lancet) on the foundational science. The originating discoverer of the core biology as a co-founder is a strong signal in this range.
Academic founders at earlier career stages (postdoctoral to early assistant/associate professor level) without established KOL networks, without major independent discovery contributions, or without direct authorship of the company's foundational technology publications. Scientific credibility is present but the founder's personal reputation does not yet independently attract investor attention.
COMMERCIAL FOUNDER APPLICATION: The Upper Range and Lower Range sub-band distinctions above apply primarily to academic founders. For commercial founders without academic KOL profiles — meaning founders whose primary credibility derives from industry operating experience, domain expertise, and commercial track record rather than from academic research or institutional affiliation — score within the 16–20 range based on: depth of domain-relevant industry experience (number of years, seniority of roles, relevance to the company's commercial challenge); demonstrated client relationship access or institutional network quality; and evidence of commercial translation capability (prior revenue-generating roles, business development track record, or documented customer acquisition at prior organizations). A commercial founder with 15 or more years of domain-relevant industry experience and documented access to the company's target customer segment may qualify for the upper portion of this range even without academic KOL credentials.

Team includes relevant scientific training but limited independent research or publication track record. Founders may be graduate students, early postdocs, or industry professionals without prior biotech leadership. No institutional board members or formal advisory structure. The team represents early potential but has not yet demonstrated the credibility signals that accelerate fundraising.

Team lacks relevant scientific or industry expertise for the company's therapeutic area. No identifiable domain expert on the founding team. No advisory board. No institutional support or mentorship relationships. The team composition does not provide fundraising-relevant credibility signals.
criterion.negative_credibility_protocol:
NEGATIVE CREDIBILITY SIGNAL PROTOCOL: Before finalizing the B1 score, the evaluator must assess whether any credibility claims made by the team — including titles, institutional affiliations, authorship or contribution claims, priority claims, and competitive positioning claims — are directly contradicted by verifiable evidence. Verifiable evidence includes: title records (LinkedIn, company website, filings); publication author lists (PubMed, bioRxiv, journal archives); public regulatory records (FDA, EMA, Companies House); and direct competitive existence data (competitor websites, press releases, third-party databases).
If one or more contradictions are identified, apply a deduction within the assigned band as follows:
SINGLE MINOR CONTRADICTION: A single instance of informal title inflation, modest overstatement of a contribution, or unverifiable but plausible claim. Apply a 1-point deduction within the assigned band. Do not drop below the band floor.
MULTIPLE CONTRADICTIONS OR SINGLE MATERIAL CONTRADICTION: Multiple contradicted claims, or a single materially false claim (fabricated institutional affiliation, false authorship claim, claimed contribution to a public law or regulatory process that is contradicted by the public record). Apply a 2–3 point deduction within the assigned band. The evaluator may drop to the next lower band if the deduction would exceed the band floor.
NO CONTRADICTIONS IDENTIFIED: No deduction. Score per band definitions on their merits.
This protocol applies regardless of whether the midpoint-default is in effect. A score at the band midpoint under the midpoint-default may still receive a deduction if contradicted claims are identified with verifiable evidence.
DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENT: The Justification field must name each contradiction, identify the source that contradicts it, and state the deduction applied. When no contradictions are found, a one-sentence statement is sufficient: "Negative Credibility Signal Protocol applied — no contradicted claims identified."

criterion.name: Scientific Foundation and Data Package
criterion.purpose: Evaluates the quality of the company's scientific foundation and data package at the discovery-to-early-preclinical stage. Measures signals that seed-stage and early-venture investors use to evaluate scientific risk: publication quality, data reproducibility, translational readiness, and lead candidate status.
criterion.non_therapeutic_application_note:
NON-THERAPEUTIC COMPANY APPLICATION — SCIENTIFIC FOUNDATION AND DATA PACKAGE: The B2 band definitions are calibrated for therapeutic life science companies and reference in vivo efficacy data, lead candidate nomination, IND-enabling studies, and peer-reviewed publication tiers grounded in biological science. For non-therapeutic companies — including bioinformatics software, genomic data infrastructure, health IT platforms, diagnostic software, and life science tools — the following analog framework applies.
The evaluator must explicitly state in the B2 Justification field that an analog framework is being applied and identify which band elements are being mapped to software-appropriate equivalents. Silent application of this framework without disclosure is not permitted.
SOFTWARE-APPROPRIATE EVIDENCE HIERARCHY (maps to B2 band definitions): Band 16–19 equivalent: Independent benchmarking study published in a peer-reviewed journal with IF above 10, conducted by a credible third-party institution on standardized datasets, demonstrating performance superiority across multiple metrics against named competitors. Company-generated validation data confirming platform reproducibility across multiple deployment environments. Clear commercial deployment pathway with documented customer validation (signed contracts, LOIs from named institutions). Band 11–15 equivalent: Peer-reviewed publication in a high-quality journal (IF above 10) validating the core algorithmic approach, even if published by academic collaborators rather than the company. Independent benchmarking data from a credible third party, even if unpublished or in pre-release form. Multiple performance metrics documented against named competitors with a defined methodology. Commercial pathway is plausible but customer validation is limited to LOIs or pilot engagement without executed contracts. Band 6–10 equivalent: Peer-reviewed publication in lower-tier journals or conference proceedings. Self-reported performance benchmarks without independent validation. Single performance metric documented. Platform is functional but commercial validation is absent or preliminary. Band 0–5 equivalent: No peer-reviewed publication. No independent benchmarking. Performance claims are unvalidated. Platform is in development without documented external validation.
When applying this analog framework, note that band elements referencing IND timelines, FDA designations, and clinical trial data are structurally inapplicable to software companies and should be excluded from the scoring basis. Score on the elements that do apply.
criterion.band: Foundational science published in a top-tier peer-reviewed journal (Science, Nature, Cell, or equivalent with IF >30). In vivo efficacy data demonstrated in validated animal models with dose-response relationships. Lead candidate nominated with defined mechanism of action. Company-generated data (not solely academic lab data) confirms platform translatability. Multiple follow-up publications or independent replication of core findings. Clear path from current data to IND-enabling studies.

Foundational science published in high-quality journals (Nature Communications, PNAS, Cell Reports, or equivalent with IF >10). In vitro efficacy data demonstrated across multiple disease models or cell types. In vivo data may be from academic labs rather than company-generated. Lead candidate not yet formally nominated but therapeutic modality is defined. Core patent filed with composition-of-matter claims. Translational pathway from academic science to therapeutic development is plausible but unvalidated.

Scientific foundation is published but in lower-tier journals or as conference abstracts only. Data is limited to a single model system or cell type. No in vivo data available. Lead candidate selection is in progress but not finalized. Core IP may be provisional or narrow. The science is promising but the data package does not yet support confident investor assessment of translational risk.

Scientific concept is unpublished or published only as a preprint. No efficacy data of any kind (in vitro or in vivo). No lead candidate identified. IP position is absent or based solely on trade secrets. The scientific foundation is insufficient to evaluate translational potential.

criterion.name: Sector and Downstream Capital Alignment
criterion.status: Revised — V.5 R2; prior revisions retained
criterion.purpose: Evaluates whether the company operates in a sector that aligns with current investor appetite and whether the downstream capital environment (Series A and beyond) is receptive to the company's therapeutic area and modality. Uses the same two-component scoring structure as A3.

component.name: Base Tier Classification
component.band: Company operates in a sector with strong downstream Series A/B appetite. Tier 1 sectors for 2025–2026: obesity/GLP-1 and metabolic therapies; antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) and targeted oncology payloads; radiopharmaceuticals; immunology/inflammation; AI-native drug discovery platforms. Platform technology with multi-indication optionality. Lead investor has demonstrated follow-on capacity for the anticipated Series A size. Delivery platforms in Tier 1 therapeutic areas receive Tier 1 classification.

Company operates in a sector with active but not peak-level downstream capital availability. Tier 2 sectors for 2025–2026: neuroscience/CNS; rare disease; gene therapy and cell therapy; cardiovascular; precision oncology (non-ADC). Series A investors in the sector are identifiable and actively deploying capital. Platform optionality may extend into Tier 1 areas.
component.sector_addition: HEALTH IT / GENOMICS INFRASTRUCTURE / LIFE SCIENCE TOOLS — TIER 2 DEFAULT: Same classification and rationale as A3. Companies providing software platforms, data infrastructure, analytical tools, or enabling technologies to the life science industry are classified as Tier 2 by default. At the Profile B raise level, the downstream capital environment (Series A and beyond) for life science tools companies is active, with a defined investor universe of specialized health IT and life science tools funds in addition to generalist life science VCs. The Tier 1 upgrade and Tier 3 downgrade conditions defined in A3 apply equally here.
component.band: Company operates in a sector with limited downstream capital options. Series A may require specialized investors. The path to $30M+ follow-on rounds is plausible but narrow.
Company operates in a sector with minimal current downstream capital interest. The path to a Series A above $15M is unclear or dependent on sector rotation.

component.name: Market-Evidence Modifier
component.instruction: Apply the same modifier thresholds as A3. After assigning the base tier score, adjust by ±2 points based on documented sector-specific M&A and capital deployment activity within the 12 months preceding the evaluation date.
component.modifier: 3 or more acquisitions exceeding $1B in the sector within the past 12 months.
1–2 acquisitions exceeding $1B in the sector within the past 12 months.
Consistent with tier classification. No adjustment.
Funding contraction or major pipeline failures within the past 12 months.
Capital withdrawal, regulatory headwinds, or pattern of clinical failures across the sector.

criterion.operational_viability_condition:
OPERATIONAL VIABILITY CONDITION: Before finalizing the B3 score, apply the following gate.
TRIGGER: If the company scores 5 points or below on BOTH B2 (Scientific Foundation and Data Package) AND B5 (Validation Signals and Early Traction), the B3 final score (base tier score plus any market-evidence modifier) is capped at 8 points.
RATIONALE: A score of 5 or below on B2 falls within Band 0–5 ("Early or Insufficient Scientific Evidence") — the rubric's definition of no verified scientific output. A score of 5 or below on B5 spans the lowest scoring bands — the rubric's definition of minimal to developing external validation. When both conditions are met simultaneously, the company has demonstrated neither minimum scientific output nor minimum external validation, and the structural reality is that sector conditions cannot be monetized regardless of how favorable they are. The cap prevents sector tailwinds from contributing a disproportionate fraction of the total score for companies that have not demonstrated capacity to compete for sector capital.
CAP VALUE: 8 points (the Tier 3 band ceiling for B3).
AND CONDITION: The cap applies only when BOTH B2 AND B5 are at or below the trigger threshold. If the company scores above 5 on EITHER B2 OR B5, the cap does not apply and B3 is scored on its merits. This prevents penalizing companies with strong scientific output that have not yet achieved external validation (or vice versa).
DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENT: When the Operational Viability Condition is triggered, document in the B3 Justification field: (a) the B2 and B5 scores that triggered the cap, (b) the uncapped B3 score that would have applied, and (c) the capped score that is recorded. When the condition is not triggered, a one-sentence confirmation is sufficient: "Operational Viability Condition not triggered — B2=[X] and/or B5=[X] above threshold."

criterion.name: Capital Efficiency and Milestone Plan
criterion.purpose: Evaluates the company's capital efficiency and the quality of its milestone plan. Measures whether the company is using capital wisely, whether milestones are aligned with use-of-proceeds, and whether runway is sufficient to reach value-inflecting catalysts.

milestone_scoring_guidance.instruction: Seed-stage and pre-IND companies commonly do not publicly disclose formal milestone plans. Absence of disclosure at these stages should be treated as Scenario A by default.

scenario.name: No Milestone Plan Disclosed — Information Gap

milestone_scoring_guidance.scenario: Treat as an information gap. Assign a midpoint score within the relevant scoring band and flag as [INSUFFICIENT DATA]. Do not score below the midpoint for this scenario alone. The absence of a publicly disclosed plan at the seed stage does not indicate poor planning; it reflects normal information constraints. (See Section 1.5 Two-Track Classification — this scenario is a specialized application of INFORMATION-SCARCE. If the evaluator has reason to believe the company has no milestone plan because the company appears pre-operational across multiple criteria, the INFORMATION-ABSENT classification may be applied with documentation.)

scenario.name: Milestone Plan Disclosed but Deficient — Planning Quality Gap

milestone_scoring_guidance.scenario: If a milestone plan is publicly disclosed but is vague, misaligned with stated use-of-proceeds, contains unrealistic timelines, or lacks connection to value-inflecting catalysts, treat as a planning quality gap. Score in the lower portion of the relevant band based on the severity of the disclosed plan's weaknesses.

criterion.band: Lean operations with below-market infrastructure costs (shared lab, incubator, university facilities, or outsourced R&D model). Runway of 2+ years from current funding at projected burn rate. Use of proceeds clearly mapped to specific, identifiable milestones that are value-inflecting for the next round (in vivo data, lead candidate nomination, IND-enabling studies). Original raise target was achieved or exceeded (oversubscription). Non-dilutive grants (NIH, SBIR/STTR, Innovate UK, ERC) supplement equity funding.

Operations are lean relative to stage. Runway of 18–24 months from current funding. Use of proceeds is directionally clear and aligned with the next value-inflecting milestone, even if specific dates are not disclosed. Capital raised is proportional to the company's development stage. Some non-dilutive funding or cost-efficient infrastructure is present.

Operations appear appropriately sized but capital efficiency signals are limited. Runway of 12–18 months. Use of proceeds is described in general terms without specific milestone mapping. No non-dilutive funding identified. Burn rate is reasonable for stage but not demonstrably lean.

Operations appear oversized relative to development stage, or burn rate is high without clear milestone justification. Runway is under 12 months. Use of proceeds is undisclosed or vague. No evidence of capital-efficient infrastructure or non-dilutive funding. Company may be in a distressed capital position.

criterion.name: Validation Signals and Early Traction
criterion.status: Revised — V.5 R1; v5.1 R2; prior revisions retained
criterion.purpose: Evaluates early-stage validation signals that predict fundraising velocity at the $1M–$15M level. Validation at this stage comes from accelerator acceptance, oversubscription signals, investor quality, founder recognition, strategic pharma engagement, and publication quality — not from clinical data or FDA milestones.
criterion.band:
Acceptance into a top-tier accelerator. The named programs — Y Combinator, IndieBio, SOSV, Petri — are examples, not an exhaustive list. Any accelerator meeting all of the following criteria qualifies: (a) acceptance rate below 5%; (b) demonstrated alumni fundraising outcomes at or above the company's target raise level; (c) active investor network with documented follow-on capital pipeline to the relevant sector. The evaluator must document the basis for top-tier classification in the B5 Justification field. An accelerator meeting the acceptance rate criterion but lacking documented investor network depth in the relevant sector may be scored in the band 6-8 range with a one-sentence explanation. Oversubscribed seed round (1.5x or more above original target) with rapid close (under 30 days). Lead investor is a top-tier VC with demonstrated biotech follow-on track record and significant fund size. Founder recognition from competitive programs (Schmidt Science Fellow, Forbes 30 Under 30, etc.). Strategic pharma engagement (mentoring program, Exchange program, CVC interest) at the seed stage. Foundational publication in a top-tier journal.
CEILING CONDITIONING: When all or nearly all of the qualifying signals listed above are backward-looking (accelerator acceptance, prior oversubscription, founder recognition programs, foundational publication, awards), the evaluator must assess whether any forward-transferable signal also supports the band assignment. Forward-transferable signals include: documented institutional investor follow-on capacity specifically committed to the company; named Series A lead engagement with term sheet discussions underway; active strategic pharma partnership conversations with documented timeline; or a recent (within 6 months) external validation milestone tied to the next funding catalyst. If at least one forward- transferable signal is present, score within the 9-11 band on merit. If no forward-transferable signal is present and all qualifying signals are backward-looking, cap the B5 score at 9 (band floor) and document the cap in the Justification field. Companies with saturated backward-looking validation but no forward-transferable signal cannot exceed B5 = 9 under this band.

Acceptance into a recognized accelerator or incubator. Seed round closed at or near target with institutional lead. Lead investor has biotech portfolio experience. Founder has received notable recognition or awards. Publications in high-quality journals. Conference presentations or poster acceptances at relevant scientific meetings.

Some accelerator or incubator participation but not necessarily top-tier. Seed round closed but may have been difficult or below target. Lead investor is a smaller fund or angel syndicate. Limited external recognition. Publications exist but in lower-impact venues. No significant strategic engagement.

No accelerator acceptance. Seed round is in progress or not closed. No institutional investor participation. No founder recognition programs. No strategic pharma engagement. Limited or no publication record.

criterion.name: Cap Table and Deal Structure
criterion.status: Revised — Concerto Finding C1; 42 Genetics Finding C-9/C-NF1; v5.1 R1
criterion.purpose: Evaluates cap table structure, round mechanics, and investor composition at the seed stage. A clean, well-structured cap table with identifiable institutional leads accelerates Series A fundraising.

strategic_coherence_assessment.instruction: Before scoring the band definitions below, the evaluator must assess whether any material post-pitch development has occurred that contradicts the company's stated use of proceeds, business model, or strategic direction as presented in its pitch materials or most recent investor communications. Material post-pitch developments include but are not limited to: strategic pivots to a different business model or market; significant layoffs affecting key functions (clinical, regulatory, CMC); discontinuation or deprioritization of the lead program referenced in the use of proceeds; announced changes to the company's core technology platform or therapeutic focus.
strategic_coherence_assessment.scoring_impact:
If a material post-pitch development is identified that directly contradicts the stated use of proceeds, the evaluator must apply a scoring penalty within the B6 band assignment. The severity of the penalty depends on the degree of contradiction:
SEVERE CONTRADICTION — The company's observable strategic direction is fundamentally inconsistent with its stated use of proceeds (e.g., pivot away from the therapeutic area or development stage that the raise is designed to fund). Apply the scoring rule as follows: (1) Default — score at the floor of the applicable band. (2) Drop to the top of the next lower band only when the non-SCA deal mechanics signals (round structure, use-of-proceeds mapping before the contradiction, prior capital efficiency, runway) independently warrant the lower band. (3) If the non-SCA signals warrant a score below the lower band's top, score at the assessed position within that lower band. A severe contradiction must always be flagged as a Top 3 Fundability Risk in Block 5 of the output, and the Justification field must explicitly state which rule (1, 2, or 3) was applied and why.
MODERATE CONTRADICTION — The company has made material changes to its strategy or operations that partially undermine confidence in the stated use of proceeds but do not fundamentally invalidate the fundraising thesis (e.g., reprioritization of pipeline assets, organizational restructuring that delays but does not cancel the stated milestones). Apply a 1-2 point deduction within the applicable band.
MINOR OR NO CONTRADICTION — The company's observable behavior is consistent with its stated use of proceeds, or any operational changes are immaterial to the fundraising thesis. No adjustment. Score the band definitions below on their merits.
strategic_coherence_assessment.documentation_requirement: DOCUMENTATION REQUIRED REGARDLESS OF OUTCOME: The Strategic Coherence Assessment must be documented in the A6/B6 Justification field for every evaluation, regardless of whether a contradiction is found. When the determination is Minor or No Contradiction, include a one-sentence statement in the following form: "Strategic Coherence Assessment: [brief description of what was reviewed — e.g., pitch materials, press releases, website, post-pitch announcements]. Determination: Minor or No Contradiction — no adjustment applied." Silent omission of the assessment is not permitted. An undocumented assessment cannot be verified and will be flagged as a format violation in any subsequent performance audit.

entity_count_benchmarks.benchmark: Typical for institutional-only seed rounds. Clean and efficient.
Typical for YC-affiliated or accelerator-sourced seed rounds with angel participation. Normal for oversubscribed rounds. Does not warrant a deduction if institutional leads are present.

Warrants a flag but is not inherently disqualifying if institutional leads with follow-on capacity are present. SAFE-stacked cap tables with more than 15 entities will require cleanup before a priced Series A round; reflect as a 1–2 point deduction within the applicable scoring band, not a structural disqualifier.

criterion.band: Cap table led by recognized institutional VCs or seed-stage life science funds with demonstrated follow-on capacity. Round structure is a priced round with standard preferred stock terms, or a SAFE with market-standard terms and a reasonable valuation cap. Founder ownership is majority (estimated 60%+ pre-option-pool). Entity count is consistent with stage benchmarks. No structural cap table issues.

band.label: Acceptable Cap Table with Minor Complexity

criterion.band: Cap table includes at least one identifiable institutional lead positioned for follow-on. Round structure may be SAFE-based without publicly confirmed terms. Entity count may exceed 15, which is typical for accelerator-sourced rounds but will require cleanup before a priced Series A (apply 1–2 point deduction if more than 15 entities on a SAFE-stacked table). Founder ownership is not publicly disclosed but estimated to be majority. No disqualifying structural issues.

Cap table is primarily angel-funded with limited or no institutional lead. Round structure terms are nonstandard or undisclosed. Entity count may be high (more than 20) without identifiable institutional anchors. Founder ownership dilution may be above normal for stage. Cap table will require significant cleanup before an institutional Series A.

Cap table has structural issues that impair fundraising: missing documentation, unresolved convertible instruments, excessive dilution, or no identifiable lead investor. Entity count is high with no institutional anchors. Score of 0 indicates a cap table that approaches the automatic disqualifier threshold.

criterion.name: IP and Technology Defensibility
criterion.status: Revised — V.5 R1; prior revisions retained
criterion.purpose: Evaluates the company's intellectual property position and technology defensibility at the seed stage. At this development level, IP expectations are lower than Profile A: licensed or developing IP is more acceptable, and the emphasis is on whether the IP estate provides a credible barrier to competition and supports the fundraising narrative.
criterion.non_therapeutic_application_note:
NON-THERAPEUTIC COMPANY APPLICATION — IP AND TECHNOLOGY DEFENSIBILITY: The B7 band definitions reference composition-of-matter patents and IP structures common in therapeutic development. For non-therapeutic companies — including bioinformatics software, genomic data platforms, and life science tools — the following application guidance applies.
The evaluator must explicitly state in the B7 Justification field that non-therapeutic IP application guidance is being used.
SOFTWARE AND ALGORITHM IP MAPPING: The composition-of-matter patent standard in the B7 bands maps to method patents and algorithm patents for software companies. A granted method patent with broad claims covering the core algorithmic approach is the software equivalent of a granted composition-of-matter patent. A filed but not yet granted patent application is treated equivalently under the band definitions regardless of claim type.
TRADE SECRETS AND PROPRIETARY DATA: For software companies, trade secrets, proprietary data formats, and proprietary training datasets that are not disclosed in patent filings may provide meaningful defensibility if they create switching costs or are not easily replicable. Score this dimension under the same band as a narrow patent (band 4–5 range) unless the trade secret provides substantially stronger protection.
CONDITIONAL IP OWNERSHIP: When the operating company holds an exclusive license to IP owned by a separate entity (e.g., a parent company, university, or foreign holding entity) rather than owning the IP directly, score the band as if the IP were owned, then apply a 1-point deduction within the band to reflect the additional investor risk of a conditional or licensed IP position. If the license contains a revenue-conditional ownership transfer (i.e., ownership transfers only upon reaching a revenue milestone), note this explicitly as it may be treated as a deal structure risk by institutional investors.
PRIORITY DATE ADVANTAGE: A long development history predating newer competitors' patent filings may provide priority date advantages in contested IP landscapes. Document the earliest known priority date and note any competitors' filing dates that postdate it as a defensibility signal.
criterion.band: Granted patent with broad composition-of-matter claims covering the lead therapeutic approach. IP is company-owned or exclusively licensed from a university with confirmed favorable terms. Freedom-to-operate analysis completed or in progress. IP estate includes multiple patent families or a platform patent with broad coverage. Genuinely novel modality with limited prior art providing natural first-mover advantage.

Core patent filed (pending, not granted) with broad claims. IP may be university-owned with a presumed but unconfirmed exclusive license. No additional proprietary IP filings by the company. Novelty of the underlying science provides some natural defensibility. Freedom-to-operate is untested. IP estate is narrow (single patent family) but covers the core platform.

Provisional patent filed or PCT application in progress. IP ownership or licensing terms are unclear. Prior art landscape has not been assessed. IP provides minimal barrier to competition. The company's defensibility depends primarily on trade secrets or know-how rather than formal IP protection.

No patent filings identified. IP position is based solely on trade secrets. Freedom-to-operate risk is unassessed and potentially high. No evidence of IP strategy. The company's technology may be easily replicable.

section.name: Standardized Scoring Output Format
section.status: Revised — V.5 R5; v5.1 R3; prior revisions retained

block.name: Evaluation Header
block.instruction: Required for every evaluation. Provides traceability metadata.
block.field: [Therapeutic area / modality / technology classification. For non-therapeutic companies (bioinformatics, health IT, life science tools, diagnostics software), use a technology or market classification rather than a therapeutic area. Document the non-therapeutic classification as a Market Context Note in Block 1.]

[List of primary source categories with numeric count or range. "Multiple" is not an acceptable count value. Use numeric counts (e.g., "Companies House filings (3)") or ranges (e.g., "LinkedIn profiles (5–10)") for each category.]

block.name: Routing Determination
block.instruction: Establishes profile assignment and scope status before any scoring begins.
block.field: [Profile A / Profile B / Out of Scope — Benchmark]

[Therapeutic companies: Discovery / Preclinical / IND-enabling / IND filed / Phase 1 / Phase 1b / Phase 2 / Phase 3. Non-therapeutic companies (software, bioinformatics, health IT, life science tools): Pre-Revenue — Research Tool / Pre-Revenue — Beta / Commercial — Pre-Revenue / Commercial — Revenue Generating / Growth Stage. Select the single most accurate value from the appropriate list. Do not apply therapeutic stage values to non-therapeutic companies.]

[1-3 sentences explicitly citing all three required inputs: (1) RAISE SIZE — state the target raise amount or note if unconfirmed; (2) DEVELOPMENT STAGE — state the development stage value assigned in the field above; (3) INVESTOR COMPOSITION — characterize the lead investor type and institutional depth. All three inputs are required. Omission of any input is a format error.]
[No / Yes — if Yes, indicate both profiles]
[In Scope / Out of Scope — Benchmark / Gray Zone — see rationale]

scope_flag_definitions.flag: Target raise falls within the $1M–$52M range. Standard evaluation applies.
Target raise exceeds $52M but is at or below $57.2M (10% tolerance). Evaluation proceeds with mandatory acknowledgment that instrument calibration may be less precise.

Target raise exceeds $57.2M, or company is publicly traded, or company is pre-seed. Evaluation may proceed as a benchmark exercise if clearly flagged. Scores should not be compared directly to in-scope evaluations.

scope_flag_unknown_raise_protocol.instruction: If the target raise amount is not publicly disclosed and cannot be confirmed through available sources, assign the Scope Flag as follows: assign "In Scope" with a conditional note if the company's development stage and total capital raised to date are consistent with the $1M–$52M range. Populate the Target Raise field with "[UNCONFIRMED — ROUTING SUBJECT TO REVISION]" and document the assumption explicitly in the Routing Rationale. If the raise target is subsequently confirmed to fall outside the $1M–$52M range or within the $52M–$57.2M Gray Zone, the Scope Flag and Routing Determination must be revised before the evaluation is used for client engagement decisions.

block.field: [Optional. Document rubric-fit considerations, non-therapeutic company classifications, scope boundary conditions, or profile assignment uncertainties that affect interpretation of this evaluation. If the company is non-therapeutic, document the sector classification and note which criteria required adaptation. Leave blank if no notes are required.]

block.name: Disqualifier Screen
block.instruction: The disqualifier screen is a gate. If any disqualifier is TRIGGERED, the evaluation terminates here. The company is classified as Out of Scope. No criterion scores, total score, fundability tier, or fundraising readiness are assigned. Blocks 3–5 are populated with "N/A — Disqualified" and the basis for disqualification. Block 6 (Footer) is still completed.
block.field: [CLEAR / NOT APPLICABLE / TRIGGERED — explanation. Mark NOT APPLICABLE for non-therapeutic companies per Section 2.3.]
[CLEAR / NOT APPLICABLE / TRIGGERED — explanation. Mark NOT APPLICABLE for therapeutic companies with no data handling regulatory exposure per Section 2.3.]

block.name: Criterion Scores
block.instruction: The following block repeats once for each criterion. Profile A evaluations use A1-A7. Profile B evaluations use B1-B7. The block structure is identical regardless of criterion. Note: v5.0 eliminates A8/B8 (AI and Platform Premium) and redistributes 3 points across A4/A6/A7 (Profile A) and B4/B5/B7 (Profile B).

criterion_score_template.format_note: Criterion ID and Name may be presented as separate fields or as a merged section header in the format "ID — Name" (e.g., "B1 — Team Quality and Execution Credibility"). Merged headers are acceptable provided both the ID and Name are unambiguous. All other fields in the criterion block must be populated as discrete fields regardless of header format.
criterion_score_template.field: [SCORED / INSUFFICIENT DATA — INFORMATION-SCARCE — description / INSUFFICIENT DATA — INFORMATION-ABSENT — description]

[2-4 sentences citing specific observable signals from the research dossier that justify the score and band assignment. Must include at least one named source, data point, or verifiable fact. Must explain why the score falls at its position within the band — not just why the band was selected. Where the V.5 protocols apply (Negative Credibility Signal Protocol for A1/B1; Operational Viability Condition for A3/B3; Two-Track Classification for any midpoint-default criterion), document the protocol outcome per the protocol's documentation requirement.]

modifier_sub_block.instruction: For criterion A3/B3 only, add immediately after the standard criterion block.
modifier_sub_block.field: [1-2 sentences citing specific M&A transactions, sector events, or capital deployment data within the 12-month lookback window]
[base + modifier] / 16 (if Operational Viability Condition was evaluated)
[NOT TRIGGERED — one-sentence confirmation / TRIGGERED — cite A2/A4 or B2/B5 scores and cap applied]
[uncapped score or capped score if triggered] / 16

score_summary.field: [Sum of all criterion scores using base A3/B3] / 100

fundability_tier.field: [Tier 1 / Tier 2 / Tier 3 / Tier 4 / Out of Scope]
[Strong Fit / Qualified Fit — Fundable / Conditional Fundability / Not Ready / Out of Scope]

tier.label: Out of Scope
tier.range: Disqualifier triggered, or instrument scope mismatch (publicly traded, pre-seed, raise above $57.2M). Not assigned for low scores alone.

fundability_tier.field: [PASS / FAIL — score falls within assigned tier range: Yes / No]
[2-3 sentences summarizing the primary factors that place the company in this tier]

data_confidence.definition: 0–1 criteria scored with INSUFFICIENT DATA flags, representing 7% or less of total weight.
2–3 criteria with INSUFFICIENT DATA flags, representing 8–20% of total weight.
4 or more criteria with INSUFFICIENT DATA flags, or more than 20% of total weight scored at midpoint with flags.
data_confidence.instruction: A MODERATE or LOW Data Confidence rating signals that the fundability tier should be interpreted with caution and that additional research is recommended before engagement. The Data Confidence rating does not change the tier assignment; it provides a reliability assessment of the score that produced the assignment.

operational_viability_summary.field: [NOT TRIGGERED / TRIGGERED — cite A2/A4 or B2/B5 scores that triggered the cap]
[NO CONTRADICTIONS IDENTIFIED / CONTRADICTIONS IDENTIFIED — X-point deduction applied; cite specific contradictions]
operational_viability_summary.instruction: This summary aggregates the outputs of the three v5.0 operational viability mechanisms (A3/B3 Operational Viability Condition; A1/B1 Negative Credibility Signal Protocol; Section 1.5 INFORMATION-ABSENT designations) at the score-summary level for fast client engagement triage. All component outcomes are also documented in the relevant criterion Justification fields; this element does not replace those per-criterion entries. OPERATIONAL indicates the company has demonstrated minimum scientific or clinical output, minimum external validation, and no credibility contradictions. MARGINAL indicates one of these conditions is weak or partially satisfied. PRE-OPERATIONAL indicates the company has not demonstrated minimum viability signals across multiple criteria and is typically associated with Tier 4 or OVC-triggered evaluations. This element introduces no score impact; it is an output-format aggregation only.

fundraising_readiness.field: [Strong Prospect / Fundable / Conditional / Not Ready / Out of Scope]
fundraising_readiness.mapping_rule: Tier 1 = Strong Prospect, Tier 2 = Fundable, Tier 3 = Conditional, Tier 4 = Not Ready, Out of Scope (Disqualified or Scope Mismatch) = Out of Scope
fundraising_readiness.field: [PASS / FAIL — label matches tier per mapping rule above]

top_3_fundability_strengths.instruction: List the three strongest signals supporting the company's ability to close a funding round. Each strength must cite specific, observable evidence from the research dossier in 2-3 sentences.

strength_template.field: [2-3 sentences citing specific observable signals from the research dossier]

top_3_fundability_risks.instruction: List the three most significant risks or gaps that could impair fundraising velocity. Each risk must identify a specific deficiency and its scoring impact in 2-3 sentences.

risk_template.field: [2-3 sentences citing specific deficiency and scoring impact]

fundraising_outlook.instruction: Must identify all four elements below. Written from the investor perspective.
fundraising_outlook.field: [1-2 sentences describing the single most impactful action the company can take to improve its fundability score]

block.name: Evaluation Footer
block.instruction: Summary line completing the evaluation. Must be consistent with all fields above.
